findings.text: Address space observer registration is exposed as an operation that appears atomic with respect to the write guard for the address space descriptor. Callers supply a subscription object and the target descriptor and observe either success or the internal failure status.

A locked lookup-or-create accessor for observer subscriptions requires the write guard to be held on entry. It reuses an existing subscription matching the requested operations when present and otherwise allocates through the operations provider, registers the result, and releases the allocation on registration failure, returning either a usable subscription or a failure indicator.

Observer lifetime management provides removal, reference release, deferred reclamation, and global synchronization. Removal invokes the optional release callback under a shared read section when still linked, unlinks under the collection guard, waits for in-flight callbacks, and drops a descriptor reference. Reference release decrements a shared count under the guard and only unlinks plus schedules deferred reclamation when the last reference goes away, with reclamation freeing through the operations provider and dropping a paired reference. A separate barrier waits for all in-flight shared sections.

Range-based observers are managed through insert and remove operations that maintain an interval collection plus a monotonically evolving sequence. Insertion ensures the collection exists, validates the operations pairing expectation, rejects empty or overflowing ranges, and requires a live user of the descriptor before taking an additional reference. When no invalidation is active it assigns a predecessor sequence and links directly; when invalidation is active it either queues for later processing or links immediately with the current odd sequence. Removal unlinks or cancels the pending queue entry, enforces ordering against concurrent invalidation start, waits when it raced an active invalidation until the sequence advances, and releases the paired reference. The locked insert variant expects the write guard already held.

Protection changes are exposed as a range fixup over a single area plus a driver that walks a contiguous span. The fixup rejects sealed areas, short-circuits when the new flag set equals the old, performs permission prechecks for transitions to no access on special mappings, adjusts memory accounting for newly writable private state, updates area flags and page protections under the write guard, propagates changes to page tables, refreshes statistics, and notifies performance tracking. The driver normalizes the address, validates alignment and bounds, holds the write guard across the walk, enforces contiguity and per-area permission and security checks, delegates to a per-area hook when present, and aggregates translation invalidations.

User entry for protection changes includes a plain variant that forwards with no key and a keyed variant that forwards the supplied key. Key allocation rejects any flag bits and any initialization bits outside the architected access mask, allocates under the write guard, applies the initial access setting, and releases the allocation if applying the setting fails. Key release frees under the write guard and reports the underlying status.

Remap work is described by a carrier that groups caller inputs, transient fault handling state, resolved area state, and derived control state. Caller inputs are the source address, old and new lengths, user flags, and optional destination. Transient state holds fault context and two unmap lists. Resolved state holds the located area. Derived state holds the absolute length difference, a populate-on-expand flag for pinned areas, a resize category, a flag recording whether the address space guard is held, an accounting count, and a flag recording iterator invalidation.

Transition to no access uses a page walk dispatch that pairs a normal entry checker with a huge entry checker and requests exclusive walk locking. The normal checker approves only when the frame permits the requested protection; the huge checker has two build configurations, one performing an analogous frame permission check and one absent.

Resize intent is represented by four mutually exclusive values: an initial invalid marker, an equal-length marker, a shrink marker for a smaller new length, and an expand marker for a larger new length.

Bulk area locking uses two conditional unlock helpers stabilized by a global mutex. The anonymous path acts only when a marker bit is set in the shared root, clears that marker before releasing the write guard so other users of the shared tree never observe it, and treats a missing marker at clear time as fatal. The file-backed path acts only when a dedicated flag is set in the mapping, releases the mapping write guard first and then clears the flag, treating a missing flag at clear time as fatal. Both rely on the marker remaining stable while the global mutex is held.

Observer and range collections serialize updates with the address space write guard for registration and structural creation plus a dedicated spin guard for list and tree mutation and reference count changes. Traversal for lookup and release uses shared read sections that allow concurrent readers while removal waits for quiescence before reclamation. Range insertion and removal hold the spin guard only around sequence and tree or queue mutation. Removal additionally orders against invalidation start and may sleep waiting for sequence advance, so callers must not hold guards needed by invalidation callbacks.

Protection updates and remap preparation observe write-guard and reverse-map ordering. Protection changes require the address space write guard across validation, area splitting, flag updates, table changes, and accounting. Page walks for permission prechecks request exclusive mode. Reverse-map guards are acquired file mapping first then anonymous object when present and released in the opposite order. Old table lookup never allocates and reports absence as null, while new table preparation allocates missing upper levels on demand.

Subscription reuse is keyed by the operations pointer under the collection guard. The shared user count saturates at its maximum representable value and reports overflow rather than wrapping. Destruction requires an empty subscription list and then poisons the collection pointer for debugging. Unregistration and deferred reclamation each pair descriptor reference acquisition with a matching drop, and unregistration requires a positive descriptor count on entry and after synchronization.

Range subscriptions treat the computed end as inclusive. Zero length and address addition overflow are rejected. A warning path rejects insertion when the descriptor has no live users. Successful insertion holds an extra descriptor reference that removal releases. Fresh subscriptions outside active invalidation start from the predecessor of the current global sequence; subscriptions created during active invalidation record the current sequence, which is forced odd, so readers can detect concurrent invalidation by comparing sequences.

Protection changes enforce contiguity, permission subsetting, and accounting. Sealed areas are rejected and identical flag sets succeed without work. Requests that would make file-mapped special areas inaccessible undergo a frame permission walk when the architecture requires it. Turning writable checks expand limits and charges memory unless already accounted, shared, huge, or marked not to reserve, with charges rolled back on failure; clearing writability can release accounting only for anonymous areas without an anonymous object. Private pinned areas becoming writable are populated to avoid later major faults. The driver rejects misaligned starts, overflowing ends, simultaneous grow directions, gaps between areas, and permission bits that exceed the allowed maximums, and it re-applies read-implies-execute per area when the personality requests it.
Table population for protection changes is needed only when operating within the write-protect fault handling path and the area uses marker-based tracking; otherwise no population is required.

Old table resolution tolerates missing or bad upper levels by returning absence without allocation, and reports absence for empty lower entries. New table preparation allocates missing upper levels and expects the final lower entry not to be a huge mapping. Batch sizing for moves returns a single entry when no batching benefit is possible, when the entry hint indicates singularity, or when the associated folio is absent or not large; otherwise it defers to folio batch accounting that respects writability. Soft-dirty state is preserved across moves by marking present and swapped entries when the platform supports it, leaving empty entries unchanged.

Entry moving is framed as an operation over a control block plus an extent and a pair of table entries for source and destination, with the source area obtained from the control block. The remainder of the transfer logic is not present in the routed span.

Resize category evolves from invalid to exactly one terminal intent determined by comparing old and new lengths: equal selects no resize, larger old selects shrink, larger new selects expand. The equal case permits a no-op when no movement is requested.

Range collection membership moves among direct, deferred-add, and deferred-remove states coordinated by an active-invalidation count and a tree-invalidating flag. With no active range the new entry links directly. With active ranges but no tree invalidation it links directly and records the forced-odd sequence. With tree invalidation it queues for later. Removal during tree invalidation either cancels a queued add or queues a deferred removal and then waits for the global sequence to advance; removal outside tree invalidation unlinks immediately.

Several misuse conditions are treated as fatal or warned. Clearing an unset bulk-lock marker, destroying a non-empty subscription collection, or observing a non-positive descriptor reference count triggers a fatal check. Insertion warns when the descriptor has no live users, when a non-invalidating path observes the invalidating flag, or when removal finds an unexpected empty tree node; the finish callback is expected whenever a start callback is provided. Protection changes fail safely on sealed areas, permission overreach, unallocated keys, and accounting exhaustion without partial updates beyond rolled-back charges.

User-visible protection control uses architected growth, access, personality, and key-mask constants. Growth direction bits are mutually exclusive and are stripped before permission computation, with down growth anchoring the start to the located area and up growth extending the end. Read-implies-execute personality adds execute when read is requested and the area allows execution. Key allocation rejects any flag bits and any initialization bits outside the access mask, reporting invalid argument, no space when exhausted, and interrupt when the guard acquisition is killed.

Range arguments are interpreted in page granularity: misaligned starts are rejected, zero length succeeds immediately, lengths are rounded up, and address addition that wraps is reported as out of memory.
